subject: Adaptive headroom scheduling & burst credit allocation — Seaforth AI
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@seaforth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Seaforth capacity profile + burst needs

Thanks Marissa/Karthik — quick context from our side before tomorrow's sync. We've modeled two peak patterns for the next quarter: (A) short intense spikes for on-demand inference (5–10 min, up to 60k tokens/min) and (B) sustained weekly batch runs (1–2 hours). Our infra team needs guidance on how Redwood's Dedicated headroom and burst credits would map to nodes and preemptible fallback thresholds.

Key asks:
- Suggested minimum reserved GPU slab to avoid user-facing tail latency during pattern A.
- How burst credits are consumed across concurrent models.
- Fallback plan if preemptible capacity isn't available in region us-west-2.

Attaching our capacity matrix (v2) for numbers. Happy to highlight specific rows on the call.

Best,
Alex Chen
Director, Platform 
Seaforth AI
[Attachment: Seaforth_capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@seaforth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seaforth capacity profile + burst needs

Alex — thanks for the matrix, looks clear. High-level notes ahead of tomorrow's call (short version):

1) Reserved slab recommendation: for pattern A with your peak token rates we recommend a baseline reserved slab sized to cover ~70% of 95th-percentile peak (this balances cost and tail risk). For your numbers that lands at ~8 GPUs (p4/rtx-class equiv).

2) Burst credit model: Redwood grants a transient burst pool that is consumed by sustained high concurrency. Credits replenish on a 24h cadence by default; we can set a shorter replenishment window (12h) for an enterprise add-on. Important: credits are shared across models in the same tenancy unless we carve dedicated buckets per model.

3) Fallbacks: if preemptible capacity is unavailable we recommend a two-tier fallback: 1) route to a lower-quantized model variant pinned to dedicated nodes (slight quality delta), 2) if still constrained, apply graceful tail throttling per-route with user-visible rate-limit headers and queueing.

I'll bring a suggested policy doc and cost delta scenarios to the call. Please flag rows in the matrix you'd like us to prioritize.

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@seaforth.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-08T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seaforth capacity profile + burst needs

Alex — following up with concrete guardrails we typically include in the deal sidecar: 

- Headroom SLA: reserved slab must be sized to sustain 70–80% of 95ppeak for 95% of days per month. Excess burst beyond that consumes credits.
- Burst throttles: short spikes (<=10 min) are allowed up to 2x reserved slab with credits; sustained spikes (>10 min) start shedding at 1.5x to protect other tenants.
- Credit replenishment: default 24h replenishment; enterprise option to accelerate to 12h at ~15% surcharge.
- Preemptible fallback: when preemptible not found within 60s, route to quantized variant with auto-notify and incremental backoff.

If Seaforth wants dedicated per-model credit buckets we can scope a separate entitlements addendum. I'll bring the pricing delta to the call — Ben can speak to margin/discounting.

- Karthik

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@seaforth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@seaforth.ai>
Date: 2027-06-08T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seaforth capacity profile + burst needs

Thanks Karthik — that helps. A few clarifying points from our finance and infra leads (copied Jordan):

- For our SLA we cannot accept >30% user-visible QOS variation due to fallbacks. Can you quantify expected increase in error rate / latency when routing to the quantized variant?
- If we request per-model credit buckets, what is the smallest granularity (min GPUs per bucket) and how does that affect unused-credit rollovers?
- Are credits transferable between regional slabs (e.g., us-west-2 <-> us-east-1) during cross-region failovers?

We'll be on the call tomorrow with our infra lead; if you could bring a short spreadsheet that maps reserve sizes to expected P95 latency and incremental cost that'd be ideal.

Best,
Alex

On a separate note: can you share your proposed autoscale policy draft so we can annotate?

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@seaforth.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seaforth capacity profile + burst needs — policy + numbers

Alex / Jordan — attaching a short policy draft and a cost/latency mapping table to use on the call. High-level answers inline: 

- Quantized variant impact: expect a 5–12% median latency improvement but a 3–8% quality delta depending on model family. We can run a 1-day eval on your sample prompt set to give tighter numbers.
- Per-model credit granularity: min bucket = 1 GPU-equivalent; practical smallest contractual carve = 2 GPUs to avoid fragmentation. Unused credits roll over on a configurable 7-day window for enterprise accounts.
- Cross-region credits: credits are region-bound by default (to avoid capacity leakage). We offer an optional cross-region pooling feature (multi-region pool) with geo-fallback rules — add-on priced.

Attachments: proposed_autoscale_policy_draft.pdf (policy + guardrails), Seaforth_capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx (updated with projected reserve rows).

Action items for our call:
- Marissa: walk the policy and recommended reserve rows (we'll highlight 3 scenarios).
- Karthik: present pricing delta for per-model buckets and 12h replenishment.
- Alex/Jordan: confirm which regions you want pooled and whether you need rollovers enabled.

We'll also offer a short-proof evaluation (1 day) on dedicated nodes to validate latency/quality tradeoffs — if you want that included in the pilot statement we can add it to the SOW.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_autoscale_policy_draft.pdf (pdf)]
